origins.section: 4.2 A Participant Hears the Outcome Only If It Joined
4.3 After an Abort, Only Abort Participants Are Asked
4.6 A Session Is Busy for the Whole Transaction

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-voucher-no-join: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-voucher-no-join: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-voucher-no-join: 4.2 says NO_JOIN means "don't tell me how this ends", and the 4.9 Votes table defines NO_JOIN as "no commit or abort call for this participant", so the voucher stays redeemed (b).
recorded.prompt:q-audit-after-pin: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-audit-after-pin: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-audit-after-pin: 4.3: once a participant votes ABORTED, the rest of the chain is offered only to AbortParticipants, and the plain monitor's "prepare never ran, it never joined, and its abort was never called" (declines counted: 0), so the answer is none (a).
recorded.prompt:q-points-commit: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-points-commit: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-points-commit: 4.4 says that once every participant has voted PREPARED the TransactionManager won't go back, that an exception from commit becomes a warning and the next commit runs, and that SendResponse, declared last, sent the approval after RecordApproval had failed; the page's example is a journal, not a points service, so the answer applies 4.4 by direct analogy.
recorded.prompt:q-ten-sessions: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-ten-sessions: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-ten-sessions: 4.6 and its summary say throughput is sessions divided by the time each transaction holds one (10/0.5 s = 20 a second), and that past that rate the queue grows until the listener's timeout drops requests, so c is correct.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-voucher-no-join:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-voucher-no-join:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-voucher-no-join:a: 4.2: "the TransactionManager calls commit or abort only on the participants that joined", and the leaky trace shows no abort reaching the NO_JOIN participant.
recorded.prompt:q-voucher-no-join:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-voucher-no-join:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-voucher-no-join:c: 4.11: "It doesn't know what a participant changed, so it believes the flags", and 4.2 says the participant "is the only one that knows what to undo".
recorded.prompt:q-voucher-no-join:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-voucher-no-join:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-voucher-no-join:d: The 4.9 Votes table says NO_JOIN gets "no commit or abort call", so the participant is not told about a commit either.
recorded.prompt:q-audit-after-pin:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-audit-after-pin:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-audit-after-pin:b: 4.9 'Who is called' says abort goes to those that joined when not everyone voted PREPARED, and 4.4 says a throw from commit is only logged as a warning, so abort is the other outcome of the votes, not a reaction to a failed commit.
recorded.prompt:q-audit-after-pin:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-audit-after-pin:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-audit-after-pin:c: 4.2 says abort reaches only participants that joined, and 4.3 says a plain participant after the abort is never prepared and never joins.
recorded.prompt:q-audit-after-pin:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-audit-after-pin:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-audit-after-pin:d: 4.9: "until someone aborts, prepare on each participant in order; after that, only prepareForAbort on AbortParticipants", so the votes are not all collected first.
recorded.prompt:q-points-commit:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-points-commit:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-points-commit:a: 4.4 refutes it: the TransactionManager won't go back on the PREPARED votes, and an exception in commit only becomes a warning.
recorded.prompt:q-points-commit:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-points-commit:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-points-commit:b: 4.4 refutes it: after an exception the next participant's commit runs, and the trace shows SendResponse's commit after the one that failed.
recorded.prompt:q-points-commit:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-points-commit:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-points-commit:c: 4.4 refutes it: SendResponse votes PREPARED READONLY in prepare, then 'commit: SendResponse' appears in the trace and it 'sent the approval after RecordApproval had failed', so it sends in commit; that it doesn't send in prepare is read from the trace, not stated outright.
recorded.prompt:q-ten-sessions:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-ten-sessions:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-ten-sessions:a: 4.6: a session keeps the Context until the last commit or abort returns, so four sessions held 2 s each finish only 2 a second; by the same logic, ten held 0.5 s each finish only 20 a second.
recorded.prompt:q-ten-sessions:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-ten-sessions:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-ten-sessions:b: 4.6: "While mux.request waits, the session's thread waits with it."
recorded.prompt:q-ten-sessions:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-ten-sessions:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-ten-sessions:d: 4.6 says Contexts "expire from the queue before any session takes them" once the wait reaches the listener's timeout, and 4.1 shows listener.process queuing the Context at once, so the timeout limits the time in the queue and the growth comes from the 20-a-second throughput (a short inference).
